{"id": "947f5643-498b-462d-89ec-4596c0c09ac4", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_KXczPMQCpKYtuFj546Z6bn", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Multiple Trails \u2013 AWS CloudTrail FAQs \u2013 AWS\",\"context\":\"### Data events\\\\n\\\\nOpen all\\\\n\\\\n#### What are data events?\\\\n\\\\nData events provide insights into the resource (data plane) operations performed on or within the resource itself. Data events are often high-volume activities and include operations such as S3 object level API operations and AWS Lambda function invoke API. Data events are deactivated by default when you configure a trail. To record CloudTrail data events, you must explicitly add the supported resources or resource types you want to collect activity on. Unlike management events, data events incur additional costs. For more information, see CloudTrail pricing .\\\\n\\\\n#### How can I consume data events?\\\\n\\\\nData events that are recorded by CloudTrail are delivered to S3, similar to management events. Once enabled, these events are also available in Amazon CloudWatch Events.\\\\n\\\\n#### What are S3 data events? How do I record them?\\\\n\\\\nS3 data events represent API activity on S3 Objects. To get CloudTrail to record these actions, you specify a S3 bucket in the data events section when creating a new trail or modifying an existing one. Any API actions on the Objects within the specified S3 bucket are recorded by CloudTrail.\\\\n\\\\n#### What are Lambda data events? How do I record them?\\\\n\\\\nLambda data events record runtime activity of your Lambda functions. With Lambda data events, you can get details on Lambda function runtime. Examples of Lambda function runtime include which IAM user or service made the Invoke API call, when the call was made, and which function was applied. All Lambda data events are delivered to an S3 bucket and CloudWatch Events. You can turn on logging for Lambda data events using the CLI or CloudTrail console and select which Lambda functions get logged by creating a new trail or editing an existing trail\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/faqs/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How can I audit deleted or missing objects from my Amazon S3 bucket?\",\"context\":\"### CloudTrail logs\\\\n\\\\nCloudTrail logs can track object-level data events in an S3 bucket, such as **GetObject**, **DeleteObject**, and **PutObject**. By default, CloudTrail records bucket-level events. To turn on CloudTrail logging for object-level events, see\\xa0[Enabling CloudTrail event logging for S3 buckets and objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/user-guide/enable-cloudtrail-events.html). Because data events are high-volume, they can generate millions of log entries per day.\\\\n\\\\nUse data events to track and audit operations on resources. For example:\\\\n\\\\n* Track Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) API operations on objects, such as **GetObject**, **DeleteObject**, and **PutObject**.\\\\n* Monitor AWS Lambda function invocations.\\\\n* Audit Amazon DynamoDB operations on table items, such as **PutItem**, **DeleteItem**, and **UpdateItem**.\\\\n* Track Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) API activity, such as **PutSnapshotBlock** and **GetSnapshotBlock**.\\\\n* Monitor Amazon Cognito API activity on user pools.\\\\n* Track Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) API operations on topics, such as **Publish** and **PublishBatch**.\\\\n\\\\nBy default, trails don\\'t log data events, and data events don\\'t appear in [CloudTrail event history](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/view-cloudtrail-events.html). To [activate data event logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-data-events-with-cloudtrail.html), add the supported resources or resource types to a trail. To view data events, [check your CloudTrail log files](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/get-and-view-cloudtrail-log-files.html#cloudtrail-find-log-files).\\\\n\\\\n**Note:** Additional charges apply for data event logging because of the high volume of events. For more information, see [AWS CloudTrail pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/pricing/)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/cloudtrail-data-management-events\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be. When these conflict with the documentation results above or with what you remember, prefer the most recent dated source.\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"AWS CloudTrail enhances logging for Amazon S3 DeleteObjects API - AWS\",\"context\":\"AWS CloudTrail, a service that provides logging and monitoring for AWS API calls, has made an enhancement to its logging for Amazon S3 DeleteObjects API. Previously, when multiple S3 objects were deleted using the DeleteObjects API call, CloudTrail logged the event as a single entry, providing information on the initiator and the bucket but not on the specific objects deleted. With this update, CloudTrail now logs both the overall DeleteObjects API call event and individual DeleteObject events for each object included in the bulk delete request. This new feature offers more detailed visibility into the deleted objects, strengthening security and supporting compliance requirements. The capability is available in AWS commercial regions\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/06/aws-cloudtrail-logging-amazon-s3-deleteobjects-api/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"AWS CloudTrail launches Insights for data events to automatically detect anomalies in data access - AWS\",\"context\":\"AWS CloudTrail Insights, a feature that helps identify and respond to unusual activity in AWS accounts, has been expanded to include data events. Previously, Insights analyzed only management events, but now it also monitors data events, enhancing the ability to detect potential security or operational issues. Insights for data events automatically detects anomalies in data access activities, such as increased delete Amazon S3 object API calls or error rates for AWS Lambda function invocations. This feature establishes normal baselines for data access patterns and alerts users when it detects anomalies, providing the relevant data events from the anomaly period for precise investigation. Users can configure alerts for potential issues and respond rapidly to threats or issues. Insights for data events is available in all regions where AWS CloudTrail is available, and additional charges apply for this feature. To get started, users should refer to the AWS CloudTrail documentation\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/11/cloudtrail-insights-data-events-detect-anomalies-access/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Uncover blind spots in AWS data plane operations with CloudTrail Event Coverage - AWS\",\"context\":\"AWS CloudTrail\\'s new feature, Event Coverage, allows users to view their data plane operations coverage at the account and organization levels in the AWS CloudTrail console. This feature helps identify gaps in logging posture by showing which AWS services and resource types have data event logging enabled and which do not. Data events enable tracking of data plane operations in AWS services, such as Amazon S3 object-level operations, to detect unauthorized access or exfiltration attempts. Event Coverage provides a centralized view of coverage across all supported data event sources and enables subscribing to data events directly from the dashboard. This simplifies closing coverage gaps, especially for organizations managing multiple accounts. Event Coverage is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS CloudTrail is supported. For more information on logging Data Events, visit the AWS CloudTrail documentation\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/aws-cloudtrail-event-coverage/\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"setting-up-cloudtrail-multi-region\",\"skill_description\":\"Enables a multi-region AWS CloudTrail trail with S3 log storage, CloudWatch Logs integration, and CloudWatch Logs Insights queries for security monitoring and compliance auditing. **Short answer:** No, not automatically for either case. S3 `DeleteObject` and Lambda `Invoke` are both **data events** in CloudTrail — which are off by default. They're only recorded if a trail has event selectors explicitly configured for those resource types. Management events (console sign-ins, IAM changes, trail/bucket-level config changes, etc.) are logged by default, but object/invoke-level data plane activity is not.

**Your 4 trails:**

| Trail | Scope | Custom event selectors? | S3 object events | Lambda invoke events |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `IsengardTrail-DO-NOT-DELETE` | multi-region, acct 012345678901_1 | No | ❌ Not captured | ❌ Not captured |
| `nebula-single-region-trail` | single-region (us-east-1) | No | ❌ Not captured | ❌ Not captured |
| `nebula-data-events-trail` | single-region (us-east-1) | Yes | ✅ Only for bucket `nebula-audit-covered-012345678901_1` (`AWS::S3::Object`, Data events) | ❌ Not captured |
| `JMERWIN_Org_Trail` | org trail, home region us-east-2, acct 012345678901_2 | Yes (per config) | Unknown — this trail lives in a different account, so I couldn't pull its event selectors from here | Unknown |

**Bottom line for your account (012345678901_1):**
- A `DeleteObject` call would only show up in CloudTrail if it happened in the **`nebula-audit-covered-012345678901_1`** bucket — no other bucket is covered.
- A Lambda `Invoke` call isn't being captured by any trail you own — none of them have a data event selector for Lambda.
- The org trail (`JMERWIN_Org_Trail`) might add coverage depending on how it's configured, but since it's owned by a different account I can't confirm its selectors from here.

If you want, I can help scope out what adding broader S3 and Lambda data event coverage would look like (e.g., all-buckets vs. specific buckets, cost implications), or check the org trail's config if you have access to the owning account.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
